sourcedFrom: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: Henry's H002 book. A takedown semi-auto .22 LR whose barrel, action and magazines stow inside the stock. Henry's own strip is the takedown itself — barrel nut off, stock takedown nut off — and the bore is cleaned from the breech with the barrel off. Page numbers here are the book's printed folios.

steps.title: Safety rotated back to SAFE
steps.action: Rotate the thumb safety on the right rear of the receiver back toward the arrow marked SAFE. Henry notes it will only go on when the bolt has been cocked, so if the lever will not move, the gun is not cocked — that is not a reason to force it, and it is not proof the chamber is empty either. Treat the rifle as loaded until the next two steps say otherwise.
steps.aside: The safety cannot be engaged on the Henry U.S. Survival Rifle unless the hammer and trigger sear surfaces are engaged by cocking the bolt.
steps.quote: At the completion of firing, or whenever a cartridge has been chambered by operation of the bolt and you do not wish to fire it, unload the firearm by Placing the safety in the “SAFE” position.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO OPERATE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE .22, unloading, p.8

steps.title: Magazine out of the well
steps.action: Take the magazine out before you touch the charging handle. The release sits inside the front of the trigger guard; press it and draw the magazine down out of the well under the receiver. Working the bolt with the magazine still in only feeds a fresh round into the chamber you are trying to empty.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO OPERATE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE .22, unloading, p.8

steps.title: Charging handle pulled back, chamber emptied
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear to throw out any round in the chamber, then look into the chamber and the magazine well to confirm both are empty. Keep your fingers clear of the ejection port while the bolt runs — Henry warns it can catch fingers as it closes.
steps.quote: Pulling the charging handle to the rear to eject any cartridge in the chamber.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO OPERATE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE .22, unloading, p.8
steps.warn: Always unload your gun when you have finished shooting, Making certain that the magazine and chamber are empty before putting your gun away.

steps.title: Rifle confirmed unloaded before takedown
steps.action: Henry opens the takedown with the same check: make sure the rifle is not loaded. Do it again here even though you cleared it a moment ago — the barrel is about to come off the action, and a round left in the chamber is still a live round with the barrel in your hand.
steps.quote: Make certain that your rifle is not loaded.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Magazine released from inside the trigger guard
steps.action: With the rifle confirmed empty, press the magazine release in the front of the trigger guard and take the magazine out if it went back in. It stays out for the whole job, and it is one of the parts that stows in the stock afterwards.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by pressing the magazine release, which can be found within the forward portion of the trigger guard.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Barrel nut spun off, barrel out of the action
steps.action: Turn the barrel nut counter-clockwise until it runs completely off its threads, then draw the barrel forward out of the action. Keep the receiver right side up the whole time: the charging handle is a loose fit and drops out of an inverted action. Wipe the threads on the barrel and the action before they pick up grit.
steps.quote: Disengage the barrel from the action by rotating the barrel nut counterclockwise until it is free of the threads and remove the barrel.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, p.9
steps.warn: Hold the receiver right side up to prevent the loss of the charging handle.

steps.title: Stock takedown nut loosened, action off the stock
steps.action: Turn the stock takedown nut in the base of the pistol grip counter-clockwise until it is loose and the action lifts off the slot at the front of the stock. Loose is enough — the nut is captive in the grip and does not have to come out. Hold the action and stock together while you turn so neither drops.
steps.quote: Disengage the action from the stock by rotating the stock takedown nut counterclockwise until it is loose and you can separate the action from the stock.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Bore scrubbed from the breech end
steps.action: With the barrel off the action, run a nylon or brass brush wet with solvent or bore cleaner through the bore from the breech end, the way the round travels. Never a steel brush. Henry wants the bore cleaned and oiled after every session, not when it starts to shoot badly.
steps.quote: Scrub with a nylon or brass brush which has been dipped in a solvent or bore cleaner. Remove the barrel from the action and clean from the breech end.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Solvent patched out, bore oiled, residue wiped before firing
steps.action: Push cloth patches through until they come out free of solvent, then run an oiled patch through to leave a film. Before the next shooting session wipe that oil back out — Henry wants the bore oiled for storage, not for firing.
steps.quote: Pass several cloth patches through the bore to remove all solvent. After removing the solvent, oil the bore with a good grade of gun oil on a cloth patch. Wipe any residue of oil before shooting.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Exposed metal wiped and filmed with oil
steps.action: Wipe every exposed metal surface and leave a light film of oil on it. After damp weather, wipe the bore and the outside metal and oil it again; after soaking rain, snow or salt spray Henry calls for a more thorough clean that goes into the action, which is the bolt removal in Deep Clean.
steps.quote: After being subjected to damp weather, thoroughly wipe the bore and wipe off the metal surfaces. Then apply a new film of oil.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, p.8

steps.title: Action lubricated before the magazine goes back in
steps.action: Put a few drops of good gun oil on the action before the rifle is loaded again. Henry recommends this before every magazine insertion, and this gun needs a free-running bolt — it will not cycle subsonic ammunition and runs best on high-velocity .22 LR.
steps.quote: Prior to inserting the magazine, we recommend lubricating the action with premium quality gun oil.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO OPERATE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE .22, p.8

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel, action, stock and magazine are now separate. That is Henry's field strip. If the action itself needs cleaning — after rain, snow or salt spray, or heavy fouling — Deep Clean follows Henry's bolt removal; otherwise move on to cleaning.
steps.quote: To clean the action, use the following instructions.
steps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, p.9

deepSteps.title: Action cocked
deepSteps.action: With the barrel off and the action separated from the stock, pull the charging handle back to cock the action. The bolt comes out of a cocked action; trying it with the hammer down only fights the hammer.
deepSteps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, cleaning the action, p.9

deepSteps.title: Magazine out
deepSteps.action: Confirm the magazine is out of the well. Henry repeats it here because the action is about to be worked by hand with the bolt coming loose.
deepSteps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, cleaning the action, p.9

deepSteps.title: Bolt pressed back, charging handle lifted out
deepSteps.action: Put your index finger into the front of the action, where the barrel was, and push the bolt rearward until the charging handle comes free, then take the handle out of its slot. The bolt is under the action springs — keep pressure on it and let it back forward under control, not with a snap.
deepSteps.quote: Insert your index finger into the front of the action and depress the bolt until the charging handle is free to be removed.
deepSteps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, cleaning the action, p.9

deepSteps.title: Action tilted forward, bolt, springs and guide out
deepSteps.action: Tip the action muzzle-end down and let the bolt, the two action springs and the action spring guide slide out of the front. Lay them out in order on a clean surface so they go back the same way. Clean the bolt face and the inside of the action, then oil lightly.
deepSteps.quote: Tilt the action forward and remove the bolt, action springs and action spring guide.
deepSteps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — HOW TO DISASSEMBLE YOUR HENRY U.S. SURVIVAL RIFLE, cleaning the action, p.9

deepSteps.title: No further disassembly — the rest is gunsmith work
deepSteps.action: Henry's book stops at the bolt. The sideplate, hammer, trigger, safety and extractor are on the parts list but the book gives no procedure for them, and Henry wants parts installed by a licensed gunsmith. Clean what is now open and go no further.
deepSteps.quote: ALWAYS LET A QUALIFIED GUNSMITH WORK ON YOUR GUN AND CHECK ANY WORK YOU THINK WAS NOT PERFORMED BY A GUNSMITH.
deepSteps.cite: U.S. Survival .22 | Instruction Manual For All H002 Series Rifles — undated — no edition or revision is printed; the only code is an unlabelled '7.20' on p.2 — GUN PARTS, p.11

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush from the breech end with a nylon or brass brush and solvent
Patch until the solvent is out, then one oiled patch
Wipe the oil out before the next session
Do not plug the barrel or store it in a fabric case that soaks up the oil

cleaning.name: ACTION & EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the barrel threads and the barrel nut
Wipe all exposed metal and leave a light film of oil
Oil the action before the magazine goes back in
Never force a stiff action — find what is binding

reassembly: If the bolt was removed: tilt the action and slide the action spring guide, the action springs and the bolt back in, press the bolt back with a finger from the front and refit the charging handle — Henry's instruction is to reverse the disassembly.
Fit the rear of the action onto the forward slot of the stock, hold both firmly and turn the stock takedown nut in the base of the pistol grip until it is firm and tight.
Line the barrel lug guide at the rear of the barrel up with the slot in the upper front of the action and turn the barrel nut to lock it. The barrel must be secured very tightly to the action.
Keep the receiver right side up throughout so the charging handle does not fall out.
fncheck: With the rifle empty and no magazine in, pull the charging handle fully back and let it go: the bolt should run home freely. Rotate the safety back to SAFE and confirm it engages on the cocked action, then forward to fire. Check the barrel nut is still tight — a loose barrel is the first thing to look at if this rifle stops shooting where it did.
